# Developer Diary - Use of AI in FishBot development

## Before FishBot v0.5.2 - early beginnings
AI usage was relatively limited:
* I used ChatGPT to explain basic concepts (particularly as I had never written any JS before I started this project), but I implemented the vast majority of the concepts in Python / JS myself to be able to internalise these & get familiar with JS's quirks quickly.
* A few low-impact functions e.g. math functions like `arrayMedian` were generated by ChatGPT, but otherwise relatively low direct interaction of AI with the codebase.

In hindsight, doing it this way allowed me to figure out (by iteration) an appropriate software architecture ("Controller Model"); this is proving to be really valuable now as I am able to change the bot's behaviour relatively easily.

## FishBot v0.5.2 - enter Claude
FishBot v0.5.2 was the first version to be assisted by **Claude (Opus 5)**, integrated into VSCode.
* Claude seemed to perform really well at implementing code with a clear, limited-scope specification. 'Plan mode' worked well for refining the spec to a relatively-limited scope task. 'Auto-mode' (after a clear specification was produced) also worked quite well and got relatively close to the solution on the first try.
* I was quite pleased with the results; there was some onboarding to do with regards to the style and architectural constraints (e.g. `hq_toc` being the sole state mutator), but otherwise, it was a similar experience to onboarding a junior engineer to a new company.

## FishBot v0.5.3 - exploring AI capabilities
In FishBot v0.5.3, I explored a more AI-forward approach where I would spec out a GitHub issue and let Claude (on Auto mode) automatically generate a fix on a separate branch. I then reviewed the PR & performed some pruning (e.g. redundant / unnecessary optional parameters) before merging, but otherwise Claude performed relatively well in this task also.

After providing it example maps from the official WZ2100 GitHub, I was also impressed by how Claude was able to one-shot support for `game.js`-defined maps in my map repackager. I did not review the code quality in this case because the script only had to run once on my machine, but it certainly did the job and I was happy with the outcome.

During v0.5.3 development, I also asked Claude to implement some telemetry: the final goal being to Ralph-Wiggum-loop and autonomously implement behavioural improvements. Ultimately, I put this effort aside after realising that FishBot (as it stood in v0.5.3) did not have enough behaviour parameterised to allow for parameter (number) tuning, so Claude would have gone in circles changing the *code* instead which almost certainly would have broken something fundamental (as well as being an inefficient use of tokens).

In hindsight - if bot's performance could be tuned numerically, a standard PSO algorithm would have been more appropriate than AI, as PSO does not use tokens. From this failure, I learned that finding the correct metrics (those most strongly correlated with win rate) is another fundamental strategic gap to fill. The game is relatively complex, so this may take some time, but I believe it is necessary to allow Claude to reach its full potential.
